Merge harmonized source tables across sources into one schema.

Source: R/merge.R
merge_sources.Rd

Each source has different patient ID columns (e.g. stay_id vs patientunitstayid). This function UNION ALLs harmonized source outputs into a single target schema (default: "rendehr"). For time series, analysis_level = "admission" reads the native-grain ts_tab, and analysis_level = "icu" reads the derived ICU projection ts_icu created by make_icu_timeline(). In the merged time-series table, src_icu_id is always the native/source ICU ID. The projection columns assigned_icu_id, event_origin, and icu_time_relation are emitted only for analysis_level = "icu" (omitted in admission mode, where they would be all NULL). The merged ehr_id is grain-specific: analysis_level = "admission" keys on src_patient_id + src_admission_id, while analysis_level = "icu" additionally appends the (assigned) ICU id. It is recomputed from the source id columns at merge time, so it always matches the requested grain regardless of how each source cohort_info was built. Use event_id to track the same physical event across admission and ICU projections.

Usage

merge_sources(
  src_names,
  db_name = NULL,
  base_dir = NULL,
  target_schema = "rendehr",
  merge_ts = TRUE,
  merge_dur = TRUE,
  merge_flat = TRUE,
  merge_cohort = TRUE,
  append = FALSE,
  analysis_level = c("admission", "icu")
)

Arguments

src_names

Character vector of source names (e.g. c("mimic_iv_demo", "mimic_iii_demo", "eicu_demo")).

db_name

Postgres database name. Defaults to the active project config, then "rendehr".

base_dir

Project root directory. Defaults to the active project config, then current working directory.

target_schema

Target schema for merged tables. Default "rendehr".

merge_ts

Build merged ts table (rendehr.ts). Default TRUE. Its value column keeps the source type, NUMERIC(18,3), as does dur's.

merge_dur

Build merged dur table (rendehr.dur) from each source's dur_tab (medication exposures, infusions, ventilation episodes). Default TRUE. Uses the same ehr_id/append-mode contract as the other merged tables; unlike ts, dur has no separate ICU projection variant, so the same source dur_tab is read regardless of analysis_level.

merge_flat

Build merged flat table (rendehr.flat). Default TRUE. Every flat column of any source is kept; it is NULL for sources that do not provide it.

merge_cohort

Build merged cohort_info table (rendehr.cohort_info). Default TRUE.

append

If FALSE (default), rebuild merged tables from exactly src_names. If TRUE, keep existing merged tables and replace rows for src_names before inserting their current data. Append mode requires the selected target tables to already exist and uses their existing columns as the schema contract.

Both modes run in a single transaction that is rolled back on error, so a failed merge leaves the previous merged tables unchanged.

analysis_level

Time-series grain to merge: "admission" merges native ts_tab; "icu" merges ts_icu and requires make_icu_timeline() first. At "admission" the merged flat and cohort_info hold one row per admission: the row of its first ICU stay (earliest ICU admission time, then lowest ICU id), or the ICU-less row when there is no ICU stay. The number of later-ICU rows left out is reported per source.

Value

Invisibly TRUE.

Details

An admission does not mean exactly the same thing in every source. In MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, src_admission_id is the hospital admission (hadm_id) and cohorts are selected per admission. In eICU it is the hospital stay (patienthealthsystemstayid), but cohorts are selected per ICU unit stay (patientunitstayid), so a merged eICU admission holds only the unit stays that were selected, not necessarily the whole hospital stay. eICU also has no admission timestamps: its window tables store offsets in minutes (admittime is 0), while MIMIC stores timestamps. Times in time_since_hadm_min count from the hospital admission in every source.

The merged ehr_id is computed as concat_ws('_', NULLIF(CAST(part AS text), ''), ...) over each row's grain-defining source ID parts (patient, admission, and — at ICU grain — ICU). concat_ws() silently omits any part that is NULL or the empty string rather than raising, on the assumption that every source row always has non-NULL values for its grain-defining ID columns. If that assumption is ever violated for a given row, its ehr_id is computed from only the remaining non-NULL parts, which could coincide with another row's ehr_id; this is a documented, currently unvalidated assumption, not a runtime-checked invariant.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
merge_sources(c("mimic_iii_demo", "mimic_iv_demo", "eicu_demo"),
              db_name = "rendehr", target_schema = "rendehr_admission")
} # }
